chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I performed the obligatory prayer but forgot to recite [the Quran] in all of my prayer.' He said: 'Did you not complete the bowing and prostration?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then your prayer is complete if it was due to forgetfulness.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Is my prayer valid if I forgot to recite the Quran entirely during it?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic principle that the validity of obligatory prayer (*salah*) rests primarily on the performance of its essential pillars (*arkān*), such as bowing and prostration, rather than the recitation of the Quran (*qira'ah*), which is often considered a recommended act (*mustahabb*) or a pillar depending on the school of thought. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between forgetfulness (*nisyan*) and deliberate omission, ruling that the prayer remains complete if the core physical acts are fulfilled, thereby offering practical ease (*taysir*) for the worshipper. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the substance of worship over its formalistic components when errors occur unintentionally.
